Kraken: Asking How Funds Will Be Used After Leaving the Platform Is Unacceptable; XMR Will Remain Listed Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi said the platform was wrong to send emails to clients who bought and withdrew Monero (XMR) using their own money, asking for information about their employer, source of funds, and intended use of the coins. He said no rule required these inquiries, and someone had flagged a client simply for being young and having substantial funds. The requests have been withdrawn, and affected clients have been told they do not need to provide anything. Sethi said asking where funds came from is reasonable, but asking how they will be used after leaving the platform is unacceptable. Kraken has removed such questions and will keep XMR listed. — link

Bitcoin Price Bets Help Push Weekly Crypto Volume on Kalshi and Polymarket to Record $2.7B Bloomberg, citing data compiled by a Dune Analytics user, reported that weekly notional volume in crypto-related contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket hit a record $2.7 billion last week, driven mainly by bets on short-term Bitcoin and other crypto price moves. Crypto now ranks second only to sports on both platforms. Crypto exchanges are expanding into prediction markets as spot volumes decline, with Coinbase's offering powered by Kalshi. However, legal challenges to sports contracts in several U.S. states could affect crypto exchanges' willingness to expand into prediction markets. — link

Highlight Clip: Arthur Hayes: High-FDV Shitcoins Can't Even Pump on Binance Anymore Arthur Hayes: High-FDV Shitcoins Can't Even Pump on Binance Anymore Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes said in an October 16 interview with LukeMartin that the entire crypto industry has abused tokenomics. From ICOs to VC private sales and presales, some projects raise funds supposedly to build products, only to dump tokens after launching protocols and unlocking allocations. Retail investors buying at TGE suffer heavy losses, sometimes watching token prices plunge 95%. Hayes argued that retail investors increasingly see through the high-FDV, low-float model, saying such tokens "can't even pump on Binance anymore." He favors projects like Hyperliquid, which have genuine product-market fit, return revenue to token holders, and avoid massive sell pressure from presold token unlocks. — link

Arthur Hayes: Maelstrom Has Closed Its Directional Positions, Taking Profits on ETH, ENA and UNI Arthur Hayes said Maelstrom has closed all positions in its directional trading book, taking profits on ETH, ENA, UNI and other altcoins. He believes the market may need to fall before rising, citing uncertainty surrounding macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions. He plans to remain on the sidelines and wait for an all-clear signal. According to @EmberCN , Arthur Hayes reduced his holdings in various tokens totaling approximately $26.08 million, including 8,000 ETH (approx. $19 million), 14 million ENA (approx. $2.76 million), and 323,000 UNI (approx. $2.24 million). — link
